title: Amazon Basics Electric Coffee Grinder, Coffee Bean and Spice Grinder, With Heavy-Duty Stainless Steel Grind Blades
description:
About this item
Electric coffee bean grinder appliance for home use
Can grind 30 grams/1 ounce of beans for drip coffee brewing in 10 seconds
Grind coffee beans, herbs, spices, grains, nuts, and more
Clear safety lid allows you to easily see the results in progress
Heavy-duty stainless steel grind blade

reviews_5s:
i keep hearing that it's best to splurge on a grinder but this was worth the buy and wasn't too expensive either. i accidentally bought whole beans and was laboring away with a pestle and mortar until my gf forced me to order this because i was taking too long in the mornings and tiring myself out early in the day. it's easy to use and cleanThis is a very basic blade grinder but it is quite effective. Because the blade appears to be connected to the end of the motor shaft, there is no extra bearing required to support the blade. As a result, the grinding cup is not removable. But since the motor bearings tend to be pretty quiet, the grinder itself is as well. It will make a bit of noise as the beans come in contact with the blade but quiets down in a few seconds. Very good grinder for the price. Cup is not quite as large as say the kitchen aid but more than enough for normal coffee grinding needs.My previous grinder broke after 2 years of usage (and it was $82 at Walmart!). This one has been good for the few months I have been using it. Would suggest you grind for 1-2 seconds less than the suggestion for your maker-type, and I make a large pot every time, so I actually have to use this twice (the size isn't quite large enough) per pot of coffee, but I am still very pleased with this product, especially for the price. If you place your hand over the entire top of grinder, the noise level isn't that bad, and the grind quality to my untrained eyes looks very consistent.Inexpensive, reliable, reasonably fine grind.

I'm using this to grind some coffee beans my daughter bought me as a gift. I didn't own a coffee grinder.

I'm also using them to grind Hibiscus flowers into a tea. One $3 bag of hibiscus flowers is going to make about $50 worth of individual Tea bags worth of hibiscus tea.

This little machine does the job in seconds. Maybe 30 seconds total?

The coffee was tasty and a reasonably even grind and this tool is much less expensive than a coffee grinder.Coffee bean grinder is nice but I bought coffee beans and the brand sent was not beans. I also purchased Amazon choice Colombian beans and it was ok. The grinder works well. I only used twice wishing I didn’t buy because I only bought for coffee pot I purchased. Not as I remember percolated coffee as a kid. Sorry I bought the Farberware pot too.I got this to grind up regular sesame seeds and black sesame seeds to get all the nutritional benefits, I’ve never bought a seed grinder before so I tried it out immediately and it seems to be working great. I’m very pleased with how convenient this will be. I recommend.BUY 4 ,,,THESE ARE GREAT LITTLE GRINDERS, GREAT FOR GRINDING ( CLOVES ). I BOUGHT 1 FOR CLOVES 1 FOR COFFEE, 1 FOR CINNAMON AND 1 TO GIFT..Bought it for my husband since the one he got for Christmas (a different brand) had broken. Seems to work fine and doesn't wake the house when he makes his coffee in the mornings.amazon basic have some good quality product at affordable price and this is one of them. I use this for dry spices and it work perfect for me.It does it's job and it's easy to clean. If you're thinking about a grinder this one is a good choice.
reviews_1s:
The design flaw with this item is that the top clear part closes with the rim going on the outside of the base while the Krups model does the opposite. So when you are grinding the beans, coffee grounds make their way to the side of the base unit. Two things happen because of this. When you go to empty the grounds, it makes a mess and if you want to grind more beans right away the power switch may not work due to the grounds collecting on the outside of the base which means you have to clean it before using.It ground okay but the button in the lid that is supposed to engage the switch to operate it was temperamental to begin with and stopped working within a few days. I would return it but can’t find the box it came in. Rather than risk another faulty one I got a Mr. Coffee grinder that was one sale fit about the same price, regularly $29, and it has been working great. I ordinarily like Amazon Basic products, but this one disappointed.
Note added: after resolving lots of other hectic life stuff and health problems that prevented me from getting out to the UPS store with many intended returns that I just ate the cost of, I decided to see if I could at least get this replaced as defective, since I’d let the refund window go by because I couldn’t find the box or packing slip for a return. Figured if I got a non-defective one, I could use it for grinding spices instead of coffee. However, when I tried to follow the links for a warranty replacement (it shipped June 29, so it’s def. too late for a return, but I did post this review originally within a week of receipt and I haven’t used it since then), the “contact customer service” link kept dumping me on a page saying that customer service is overwhelmed right now and I couldn’t get any further in the process. It’s only $17 but I’ve been a really good Amazon customer this year (bought over $3000 in household stuff this summer alone, from expensive bike locks to inflatable hot tubs, door locks, flat-pack cabinets and outdoor gazebos), as well as a bunch of electronics from winter into spring, and I was hoping they’d be a little more available to help me get my money’s worth.The problem with this grinder is where the power button is and how it's activated. The lid of the grinder has large slide button that is supposed to turn the grinder on when pushed down, the problem is this slide works by moving a small nub down to make contact with the button on the base. What seems to happen after every use is the button gets blocked by coffee grounds which prevents the plastic nub on the grinder lid from making contact with the button. A coffee grinder is not something I would clean often but with this one you really have no choice.

It's also extremely messy probably because the lid is a little to big for the base.

Also I noticed an electrical smell when grinding for a fine grain.

Do yourself a favor spend the extra 10 bucks for a grinder with a better design.Issue #1 - the lid is designed to jam at an awkward angle more often than to fit in the closed position. Once closed, there is so much slack and wobble, one has to look to make sure it is actually closed.

Issue #2 - upon opening the grinder, one is met with an overpowering odor of machine oil and plastic out-gassing. You will need to clean it thoroughly and air it out before using it. This will not be easy given the close quarters and sharp un-removable blade in the middle.

Issue #3 - the power cord was designed by someone with special needs and no clue about basic design principles. It seems intentionally designed so the cord will always be caught under the grinder, preventing it from sitting flat. And the incorporated storage 'feature' for the cord is preposterous and simply does not work. So after tediously winding the cord, it immediately unwinds when you let go if it.

Issue #4 - I live in a small town, and the nearest Staples is more than a 30 minute drive from me. Yet the ONLY way I can return this piece of garbage WITHOUT having to pay for the 'privilege', is to drop it as a Staples store. If I want to use a UPS drop, i have to pay fort it.

If you dislike someone, get this for them. Otherwise, don't get this.If I could give zero stars I would.
It lasted a month😡
I ordered it April 14th
It's May 15th
And the button you push to grind stopped working.
My husband and I had a coffee grinder for almost 15 years before it wasn't sharp enough to really work well before this one.
Garbage don't waste your time.Bought this and the first time I used it, it worked fine. On our second attempt, the unit failed to even start. We attempted to use other plugs, but still nothing. Seems expensive for a single use grinder.Grinding function works alright but the lid is not well designed and allows grounds to escape the hopper, making a mess. Worth it to spend the extra money for a better product.This is ONLY for coffee beans. I bought it to grind flaxseeds and spices, which the online description includes, but the manual specifically stated, "Do not use on any other food items".Awful product-it barely grinds the coffee beans down to a fine amount, it leaves coarse pieces and results in diluted coffee. A regular blender works betterThe top switch failed before 30 days. I opted for a model from WM with a side mounted switch.
I don’t know if it will be any better but this model was the worst one we’ve had. The switch mechanism should be more robust/reliable.
